thread:
alex: :rotating_light: Alert — Canary for runtime v2.7 + model-encoder-v3 is showing 3xx/5xx spike and latency degradation on hosted region-us-west-2. Noticing increased tail latency since 2030467800.

oncall-bot: Paging oncall (sara) for incidents/timeout-errors > 5% for 10m. Incident ID: INC-2030467.

sara: I'm on it. Can someone post the quick summary (which deploy, which flag)?

michael: This was a gradual rollout. Route 40% traffic to encoder-v3 via feature flag ff:model-encoder-upgrade. Canary was at 5% earlier, we bumped to 40% at ~2030467000 to accelerate.

dana: Perf graphs — CPU on dedicated pool encoder-gpu-1 jumped to 98% on 3 pods, error rate primarily from streaming timeouts and repeated reconnects. Backend logs show: `grpc: deadline exceeded` and `kv-cache miss flood`.

alex: @sara immediate mitigation options: 1) flip ff:model-encoder-upgrade -> off (kill-switch) 2) rollback traffic to model-encoder-v2 3) scale dedicated pool (spin new instances). We should pick 1+2 now.

sara: Agreed. @deploy-bot can we toggle the flag with safe rollout? I want it off immediately.

deploy-bot: Received toggle request: ff:model-encoder-upgrade -> off. Executing.. (safety: immediate)

deploy-bot: SUCCESS — ff:model-encoder-upgrade set to OFF across regions (propagation ~15s). :white_check_mark:

csm-liz: Heads up — 2 customers reported degraded transcripts to support within last 6m (CS ticket 3247, 3248). They might be impacted while we stabilize. I'll triage customer-facing comms.

infra-jen: Turning the flag off reduced error rate but tail latency still elevated. Looks like some requests are stuck in the runtime KV cache thrash and backend connection pools are saturated. We need a traffic drain and then a service restart for the affected nodes.

alex: Ok, plan: do a rolling drain of the 3 hot pods, restart runtime process, verify kv-cache warm-up, then move traffic back if healthy. Who will run rolling drain?

sara: I'll coordinate. @michael can you prepare the drain commands and smoke checks? @qa-lee prepare quick synthetic tests for top-10 customer prompts.

michael: Drain commands (will run now):
```bash
# mark pod as draining
kubectl annotate pod encoder-gpu-1-abc drain=true --overwrite
# wait for in-flight requests to finish (30s)
kubectl exec -it encoder-gpu-1-abc -- pkill -USR1 runtime && sleep 30
# restart runtime process
kubectl rollout restart deployment/encoder-runtime -n prod --cascade=none
```
I'll run for pod 1 then 2 then 3 with 2m gap.

qa-lee: Synthetic checks ready: 1) latency < 250ms median 2) no 5xx for 2m 3) correctness quick diff on golden prompts.

(5m pass)

dana: After restarting pod-1 and pod-2, metrics improved but pod-3 still shows high reconnect rate. There's an orphaned long-lived connection causing backlog.

alex: Can we evict pod-3 and drain traffic off node? If necessary, force-delete and let scheduler reconstruct.

infra-jen: Doing `kubectl delete pod encoder-gpu-1-ghi --grace-period=30 --force`. Also increasing evictions on node gpu-node-17.

deploy-bot: Pod eviction triggered. New pod scheduled on gpu-node-22.

(4m)

sara: Post-eviction metrics look stable. Synthetic checks by @qa-lee show median latency 180ms, no 5xx in last 3m.

qa-lee: Validations: golden diffs show < 0.5% variance — okay.

michael: Rolling traffic back: moving 20% traffic to encoder-v3 for validation, will observe for 10m, then decide.

csm-liz: I've notified impacted customers: initial note about degraded experience and we're rolling mitigation. Asked for follow-ups if they still see issues.

sara: Important note — the automated rollback didn't kick earlier because our canary metric used error-count absolute, but errors were clustered on a single node and didn't exceed threshold. Filing postmortem item: canary metric needs per-pod tail latency and error-rate aggregation.

alex: Good catch. Add: fallback policy should consider kv-cache miss ratio and connection errors.

michael: At 20% traffic encoder-v3 looks fine. Increasing to 40% for 5m smoke.

(6m)

dana: Wait — as traffic rose, we saw a slow creep in CPU again on the new pod. Could be workload pattern difference. Suggest we keep encoder-v3 at 20% while we collect traces and run a targeted heap/profile.

alex: Agree. We're going to pause rollout and keep flag OFF historically but route steady 20% to canary via manual routing for controlled validation. Action items:
- sara: coordinate canary routing & keep kill-switch available
- michael: collect perf traces from the new pods and upload to S3 location `s3://redwood-inference/tmp/inc-2030467/`
- infra-jen: add temporary autoscale +1 for dedicated pool to blunt spikes
- qa-lee: run extended synthetic validation for 30m
- csm-liz: follow-up to customers with ETA for final status

sara: I'll keep incident open and update status in PagerDuty. Setting severity to SEV2 because some customers were impacted but mitigation in progress.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2030467 status: acknowledged by sara. Severity: SEV2. Oncall: sara.

michael: Uploaded traces and flamegraphs to `s3://redwood-inference/tmp/inc-2030467/traces.tar.gz`. Highlights: encoder-v3 shows hot path in attention kernel when sequence length > 1024, causing unexpected memory pressure and context-switch thrash.

dana: Repro steps captured. Will open an invariant issue for model-encoder-v3 config and quantization profile.

alex: From postmortem POV — root causes: premature traffic increase, canary metric gap (node-local errors), and insufficient autoscale buffer. For immediate runbook updates: add per-pod error-rate alert and require manual signoff for >20% rollout until autoscale tested.

csm-liz: Customers informed that service restored and we're validating. Keeping them in loop.

qa-lee: Extended validations passed at 20% for 30m. No regressions detected.

sara: Closing mitigation phase. Will keep monitoring and will schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow. If any new regressions, re-open with thread INC-2030467. Thanks all for quick coordination.

alex: Great job. I'll draft the incident summary and action items. (reacts :thumbsup:)

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2030467 marked as monitoring. Last update at 2030469735.
